blocking_findings.class: public behavior divergence — C2 contract API ordering
blocking_findings.statement: GET /api/workspaces/:id/items returns rows from 'SELECT * FROM item WHERE workspaceId=?' with no ORDER BY and no in-memory API ordering (server/app.ts line 64). None of the three contract modes produces the contract order at the API. Runtime-verified on the pristine seed the returned order only coincidentally equals updated_desc (seed insertion order); after PATCH /api/items/wi_108 the API still returns the insertion order instead of moving wi_108 first, and ?sort=updated_asc / ?sort=title_asc always return the insertion order instead of the contract seed orders (updated ascending: wi_108, wi_101, wi_105, wi_107, wi_102, wi_104, wi_106, wi_103; title NOCASE: wi_108, wi_105, wi_101, wi_106, wi_103, wi_102, wi_104, wi_107). This also removes preserved baseline list ordering (baseline server/app.ts orders 'updatedAt DESC, id COLLATE BINARY ASC'; runtime baseline probe reorders correctly after the same PATCH). The unchanged original suite still passes only because the pristine seed insertion order coincides with baseline order — a masked regression, not equivalence.
blocking_findings.evidence: probe alt FAIL lines (updated_asc, title_asc, post-PATCH updated_desc, post-PATCH title_asc); baseline probe PASS post-PATCH; diff of server/app.ts line 60 vs line 64
blocking_findings.rule: contracts/C2-item-list-sort-toggle.md bullet 1 and 2; baseline-spec.md items list ordering; scope rule 'preserve unrelated behavior' (baseline ordering is pre-existing same-endpoint behavior)
blocking_findings.fix: bounded: implement the three orderings in server/app.ts (see R2-D2 fix — same change)

blocking_findings.class: appointed strategy not implemented — material-difference requirement
blocking_findings.statement: The frozen pre-appointed requirement is a materially different API implementation that performs ordering in memory AFTER the authorized workspace-item selection, with explicit comparison matching the public SQLite NOCASE and timestamp/id tie rules, and not merely SQL ORDER BY for the new modes. The r2 alternative performs no API ordering at all: it removed the baseline ORDER BY and re-sorts in the BROWSER (src/main.tsx load()). The author's own evidence concedes this: REVIEW_RESPONSE.md 'Implemented in-memory sorting in src/main.tsx after fetching items from the server', CHECKS.md 'Sorting is performed in-memory on the client side'. A client-side sort cannot satisfy the C2 API contract (R2-D1) and is not the appointed API strategy; the revision is therefore not an acceptable materially-different API alternative in its current form.
blocking_findings.evidence: server/app.ts line 64 (no ordering); src/main.tsx lines 60-71 (client sort); REVIEW_RESPONSE.md; CHECKS.md line 2
blocking_findings.rule: role-prompts/original-preappointed-alternative.txt paragraph 2; role-prompts/clean-alternative-author.txt paragraph 2 (frozen before either original construction)
blocking_findings.fix: bounded (same change resolves R2-D1 and R2-D2): in server/app.ts items GET, after the authorized workspace() membership check, fetch rows WITHOUT ORDER BY and sort the resulting array in memory with explicit comparators: updated_desc = updatedAt DESC (ISO-UTC strings compare chronologically lexicographically), tie id BINARY ASC; updated_asc = updatedAt ASC, tie id BINARY DESC (the delivered client comparator gets this tie wrong — id ASC, see R2-O1); title_asc = SQLite NOCASE semantics, i.e. fold ONLY ASCII A-Z/a-z (0x20) then BINARY compare, tie id BINARY ASC (toLowerCase() is not NOCASE — see R2-O2). Keep the invalid-sort 400 and 401/404 precedence as delivered. In src/main.tsx remove the client-side re-sort so the UI renders API order; keep the sort selector, [sort]-triggered refetch and lifetime gates as delivered.

optional_findings.severity: optional (must be fixed as part of R2-D1/D2 work)
optional_findings.statement: Client updated_asc comparator ties on id ASCENDING (binary(b.id,a.id)*-1); the contract pins id DESCENDING for updated_asc. Empirically confirmed on synthetic tie data: got wi_z,wi_a,wi_b,wi_c; contract expects wi_c,wi_b,wi_a,wi_z. Invisible on the seed (no shared updatedAt) but a genuine contract divergence.
optional_findings.rule: contract bullet 1: 'updated_asc sorts updatedAt ascending, id descending'

optional_findings.severity: optional (must be fixed as part of R2-D1/D2 work)
optional_findings.statement: title comparator uses String.toLowerCase() + binary compare, which is NOT SQLite NOCASE for non-ASCII titles. Runtime counterexample (synthetic SQLite, supplied better-sqlite3): NOCASE orders [ss, Ä, ß]; the delivered comparator orders [ss, ß, Ä]. NOCASE folds only ASCII A-Z; a compliant explicit comparator must fold exactly those bytes.
optional_findings.rule: contract bullet 1: 'title_asc sorts title using SQLite NOCASE semantics'; appointment: 'explicit comparison matching the public SQLite NOCASE ... rules'
